subject: Initial DPA & Subprocessor Disclosure — scope and execution
messages:
From: Sofia Torres <s.torres@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-03-01 15:22 -0700
Subject: DPA & subprocessors — request for template and list

Hi Marissa,

We're kicking off contracting for an initial pilot with Redwood and our procurement team asked for a copy of your Data Processing Addendum and the current list of subprocessors. Can you send over your standard DPA and a CSV or spreadsheet that lists subprocessors, locations, and purpose?

Scope notes: the pilot will include EU resident data for a subset of users, so please flag any processors that rely on non-SCC transfer mechanisms. Also confirm whether Redwood relies on any US-based analytics or monitoring vendors that may ingest logs.

If you prefer, we can accept a redline in PDF via our legal system. We aim to have the DPA executed via DocuSign.

Thanks,
Sofia Torres
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corp

Attachments: none

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-01 16:05 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA & subprocessors — request for template and list

Hi Sofia — thanks for the note and welcome.

Looping in Rishi (legal) and Laura (sales ops) — Rishi will share our standard DPA and the current subprocessor disclosure. We do use SCCs for EU transfers by default and track subprocessor locations in the attached CSV.

Next steps we propose:
- Rishi to share DPA + subprocessor list (today)
- Acme legal to provide redlines (if any)
- We’ll review and either accept or propose narrow counterpoints; target execution via DocuSign.

If there are specific data categories or retention concerns you want to call out up front, send them over and we’ll ensure the scopes align.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Torres <s.torres@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-02 09:12 -0700
Subject: Redwood DPA and subprocessors list (attached)

Sofia — attaching our standard DPA (redwood_DPA_template_v1.docx) and the subprocessor disclosure (subprocessor_list_20260228.csv). Summary of key points:

- Transfers: We process EU personal data and rely on EU SCCs for transfers from the EEA to the US. We can provide executed SCCs as part of the final package.
- Subprocessors: Major categories are cloud infra (AWS regions: us-west-2, eu-west-1), observability (log ingestion redacted; vendor: Loglytics Inc., vendor processes only aggregated telemetry), and managed GPUs for dedicated deployments (partner vendor in APAC for private deployments on request). Full list in CSV.
- Data types: We treat API inputs and generated outputs as customer content; logs are retained for X days and access-controlled. If Acme requires different retention for pilot, let us know.

Please review and send any redlines. We are generally comfortable with most mutual edits; any requested changes that expand transfer scope or introduce atypical obligations may need legal review.

Attaching the files now.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_DPA_template_v1.docx (DPA template), subprocessor_list_20260228.csv (current subprocessors)
From: Dan Reed <dan.reed@acme-corp.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-03-03 10:45 -0700
Subject: Acme redlines to Redwood DPA

Rishi/Marissa — attaching Acme’s marked-up DPA (Acme_redlines_20260302.pdf). High-level:

- We redlined Section 4 (Subprocessors) to require 30 days prior notice and an opt-out right for subprocessors that perform certain functions (analytics/monitoring).
- We propose a specific clause for data localization during the pilot: any EU resident personal data must not be transferred outside the EEA unless covered by SCCs and with notice.
- We clarified liability caps (we trimmed Redwood’s proposed cap for gross negligence).

We can be flexible on some language if you can provide confirmation around which vendors process logs and whether logs contain identifiable data. Also prefer DocuSign execution. Please advise next steps and timeline.

Thanks,
Dan Reed
Legal Counsel — Acme Corp

Attachment: Acme_redlines_20260302.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Dan Reed <dan.reed@acme-corp.com>, Sofia Torres <s.torres@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-04 08:31 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme redlines to Redwood DPA — responses and DocuSign

Dan/Sofia — thanks for the marked-up PDF. Quick responses inline:

1) Subprocessors: We can accept adding a 30-day notice requirement for new subprocessors, but we cannot offer a broad opt-out right that would permit blocking critical infrastructure providers (e.g., cloud infra). We propose the following compromise: 30 days notice + a right to object limited to new subprocessors whose function would cause data to be processed in a materially different manner (e.g., additional downstream analytics). If you object, we’ll discuss mitigation or temporary suspension for the pilot.

2) Localization: We confirm SCCs will be applied for transfers from the EEA. For the pilot, we will ensure that production processing for EU resident personal data occurs in eu-west-1 unless you need a specific dedicated deployment (which would be a dedicated capacity/private deployment conversation).

3) Liability cap: We are open to a mutuality adjustment; our standard approach is to proportionally reduce caps for claims tied to privacy breaches. Rishi to propose revised language in-line in the attached DPA and prepare a DocuSign envelope for signature once we have final redlines.

DocuSign: I’ve initiated an envelope and will send to the signatories once we finalize the language. Temporary link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/envelope/0a1b2c3d (will be replaced by final envelope).

Can Acme confirm whether the opt-out right request is limited to analytics/monitoring vendors or broader? That will help finalize the compromise language.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed_DPA_responses_draft.docx (inline comments)
From: Sofia Torres <s.torres@acme-corp.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: dan.reed@acme-corp.com, legal@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-03-06 09:11 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme redlines to Redwood DPA — executed copy

Rishi/Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and clarifications. Acme accepts the compromise on subprocessors (30-day notice + objection limited to analytics/monitoring and other downstream processing vendors). We confirm the localization approach for the pilot (eu-west-1) is sufficient.

We reviewed your revised liability language and it is acceptable for the pilot. Rishi: please send the final DPA via DocuSign.

We’ve now executed the agreement on our side; attached is the signed copy for your records. Please countersign and return the fully executed PDF.

Regards,
Sofia Torres
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corp
